answer: A vault-backed stake makes Sybil attacks expensive: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit in a shared vault, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove fraud. A trellis of mutual attestations then links each agent to verifiable work history, so an identity with no trusted connections earns trust slowly. The old fable of free identities dies here, because every fake must pay the same stake and risk the same slash, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand stakes.
